title: RESPONSIBLE · The hidden costs of AI

slides.name: 1 · The hidden costs of AI

params.text: Understanding the environmental and ethical impact of AI

slides.notes:
AI AWARENESS DAY 2026 · Starter 4 · Principle: RESPONSIBLE · 5 minutes

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
· Understand that AI has significant environmental impact
· Learn about data centre energy and water consumption
· Consider when AI use is and isn't justified

TONE — from the teacher pack, and it matters here more than anywhere:
Avoid doom-and-gloom. Frame this as informed decision-making, not guilt. The goal is thoughtful use, not complete avoidance. AI also has POSITIVE environmental applications — climate modelling, grid efficiency — and it is worth saying so.

slides.name: 2 · Statement · frame

params.text: Every time you use AI, it uses electricity and water. Should we care?
Talk to the person next to you — 60 seconds

slides.notes:
A scale rather than a poll — this is a question of degree, and the spread is the discussion. Show the distribution and ask someone at each end to explain their position.

Watch for the room talking itself into guilt. Redirect: the useful question is not "should I feel bad" but "when is it worth it".

DISCUSSION PROMPTS
→ Does knowing about AI's environmental impact change how you'll use it?
→ When is using AI worth the environmental cost?
→ What might you use instead of AI for simple tasks?

slides.name: 3 · What's under one question

params.text: of all global electricity goes to data centres — doubling by 2026
AI's 2025 footprint, CO₂ equivalent — about New York City's
as much CO₂ as five cars over their entire lifetimes
AI data centres could use as much this year as the global bottled water industry
Nature Sustainability 2025 · International Energy Agency 2025 · MIT

slides.notes:
REVEAL ONE LAYER AT A TIME — press → for each. The room should be guessing how far down this goes.

Start by pointing at the line above the waterline: that is all anyone sees when they use it. Everything below is the same single answer.

The water layer is the one students remember, because nobody expects computing to be thirsty. Save it for last, which is where it is.

The range on the third tile (32.6–79.7) is not vagueness — it is honest reporting of a genuinely uncertain measurement. Worth naming if anyone asks why it is not one number.

slides.name: 4 · So — should we care?

params.text: Small individual actions combine into massive collective impact.
AI's total footprint is equivalent to a small country's emissions.
It lets you judge when AI is actually worth using.

slides.notes:
Reveal one at a time.

Card 4 is the one that keeps this starter honest. Say it clearly and do not let the room leave thinking they have been told off for using a chatbot.

Cost-benefit, if it comes up: complex research, accessibility needs and real productivity gains can justify the cost. Simple questions you could answer yourself, and trivial entertainment, mostly do not.

slides.name: 5 · When is it worth it?

params.text: A question you could answer yourself
Categories and ordering from the AI Awareness Day teacher pack

slides.notes:
THE POSITIONS ARE ARGUABLE AND THAT IS THE EXERCISE. The teacher pack names these categories and says which end each belongs at; it gives no numbers. Do not defend the exact spots.

Best use: ask the room to move one. "Which of these is in the wrong place?" gets further in ninety seconds than any amount of explaining, and the argument is always about the middle one.

The question underneath, from the pack: is AI the most efficient tool here, or would a simple search have worked?

Keep the tone off guilt. This is a slide about judgement, not abstinence.

slides.name: 6 · Statement · frame

params.text: Who should be responsible for AI's carbon footprint?
Extension — if you have longer than five minutes

slides.notes:
HIDDEN BY DEFAULT — the teacher pack's sub-question.

The poll is the lesson: rooms split three ways and then discover the answer is "all of the above". Take the vote before you reveal the next slide, and let the room notice for itself that everyone picked somebody else.

slides.name: 7 · All of the above

params.text: They build and profit from AI systems.
They set regulations and energy policy.
We choose when and how much to use AI.
Responsibility is shared along the whole chain.

slides.notes:
Extension — unhide together with the question before it.

LAB — SlideForge shows 6 cards here; the lab's cards take four a slide, so the rest are in these notes: Companies should — Use renewable energy, improve efficiency, be transparent.; And users can — Use AI thoughtfully, advocate for sustainability, stay informed..

slides.name: 8 · Two words worth knowing

params.text: A facility housing thousands of servers. AI needs massive ones, consuming electricity for computing and water for cooling.
Total greenhouse gases caused by an activity — for AI: electricity generation, hardware manufacturing and cooling.

slides.notes:
Both definitions were in the teacher pack only.

The water point surprises people every time. Servers generate heat; heat has to go somewhere; evaporative cooling is how it goes.

slides.name: 9 · Using AI responsibly

params.text: Five habits — none of which is "stop"
Do you really need AI for this task?
Simple questions often don't need AI at all.
Group your requests rather than sending many small ones.
Some companies use far more renewable energy than others.
We need to know AI's true environmental cost.

slides.notes: Reveal one at a time. If you are short of time, end here.

params.text: Every choice we make about technology has consequences. Use AI thoughtfully.

slides.name: 11 · Section · If any of this affected you

params.text: If any of this affected you
You will not be in trouble for asking for help.

slides.notes:
Say this out loud rather than leaving it on the slide.

Your tutor, head of year or safeguarding lead is available to help — name the actual person if you can.

From the teacher pack, the three messages that matter most:
· If you are targeted by deepfake abuse, it is NOT your fault.
· Creating AI-generated intimate images of anyone is illegal.
· You will NOT be in trouble for reporting — we are here to help.

Have the safeguarding details ready to share privately with anyone who comes to you afterwards.
